assumptions: finArea_m2 = 0.015: plausible total pectoral lifting area for a 0.25 m adult; gives stall speed ~8.95 m/s.
CLmax = 1.0: moderate value in the range reported for flying-fish wings, not extreme.
LD_max = 5: conservative glide ratio, well below any bird/glider bound.
airspeed_m_s = 12: above the stall speed 8.95 m/s at CLmax, so L=W is reachable with CL≈0.556 < CLmax.
glideDistance_m = 4: below the energy bound LD_max*glideHeight_m = 5 m for an unpowered glide from 1 m.
drag_coefficient = 0.1111 = CL/LD at the 12 m/s trim point (CL≈0.556).
drag_area_m2 = 0.001667 = CD*S; drag at 12 m/s is ≈0.147 N, so W/D = 0.736/0.147 ≈ 5, matching LD_max.
powered=false added alongside flight_mode glide to make the unpowered declaration explicit.
Omitted metabolic, thermal, swimbladder and energy-budget keys because the brief does not fix them; adding invented values would risk false violations.
final.notes: I couldn't call lean_check from here, so nothing was actually run through it. I checked consistency by hand: lift equals weight at 12 m/s, the airspeed is above stall, drag matches LD_max, and glide distance is within LD×height. C14 and E3 are out of scope because the design declares an unpowered glide. Laws whose inputs I left out, such as the metabolic, thermal and swimbladder ones, will return cannot-evaluate. No law blocks the brief.

assumptions: finArea_m2=0.01: plausible total pectoral lifting area for a 0.25 m fish; gives stall speed ~10 m/s.
CLmax=1.2: moderate value for a cambered fin wing.
LD_max=10: modest glide ratio, so max unpowered range from 1 m is 10 m.
airspeed_m_s=15: above the 10 m/s stall speed, so lift can support weight (CL≈0.53 < CLmax).
glideDistance_m=8: below the LD_max*glideHeight_m=10 m ballistic/glide bound.
drag_coefficient=0.0534 (based on finArea) and drag_area_m2=0.000534: set so D=W/LD at 15 m/s (CL/CD≈10).
powered=false added alongside flight_mode glide to make the unpowered declaration explicit.
g=9.81 m/s2 assumed for weight.
parsed.notes: I know of no law that blocks the brief. I haven't run lean_check, so the design is checked only by hand. Hand checks: lift balances weight at 15 m/s, speed exceeds stall, range does not exceed LD*h, and drag is consistent with L/D. A glide from 1 m cannot be longer than LD*h. Real flying fish glide much farther, but only by powered taxiing, which the brief excludes. The aerobic laws C14 and E3 are out of scope for an unpowered glide, so they won't be evaluated. Inputs for the swimbladder, thermal, and energy-budget laws are deliberately omitted, so those laws will return cannot-evaluate or out-of-scope.

assumptions: finArea_m2=0.015: total pectoral lifting area, wing loading ~49 N/m2, plausible for a 0.25 m flying fish.
CLmax=1.2: moderate maximum lift coefficient for a fish fin wing.
airspeed_m_s=10: above stall speed (~8.2 m/s from W=0.736 N, S, CLmax), so required CL ≈ 0.80 < CLmax.
LD_max=8: glide ratio; bounds glide distance from 1 m at 8 m.
glideDistance_m=5: below LD_max*glideHeight_m = 8 m.
drag_coefficient=0.1: equals CL/LD at 10 m/s (0.80/8).
drag_area_m2=0.0015: drag_coefficient*finArea_m2.
powered=false: added explicitly alongside flight_mode glide so C14/E3 are out of scope.
wind_along_track_m_s=0: still air assumed.
flight_duration_s=0.5: glideDistance/airspeed = 5/10.
parsed.notes: I ran no check, so I haven't confirmed any verdicts. By hand, the numbers are consistent: airspeed is above stall speed, glide distance is within LD_max times the launch height, and the drag terms agree. A real flying fish glides much farther than 5 m, but that relies on powered taxiing and wind or wave lift, which this unpowered 1 m launch excludes. C14 and E3 are out of scope because the glide is unpowered. I don't know of any law that blocks this brief.
